question: Why did Charlie Chaplin burn the negative of a feature he had paid to make?
answer: To settle a tax question. A Woman of the Sea, directed by Josef von Sternberg in 1926, was shelved after a single preview. In 1933, with the tax authorities examining his finances, Chaplin had the negatives burned on 21 June before witnesses, so its cost could be written off as a total loss.
move: When a thing is worth more destroyed than kept, expect it to go.
ask: What do I own that is worth more to someone if it disappears?
source: Robinson, Chaplin: His Life and Art
reference: Robinson, Chaplin: His Life and Art, McGraw-Hill, 1985
